operative_clauses.judgment_reason: corrected-6: Enacting words and new sec. 6 of Civil Service Rule II (excepted employees when classified): a person holding a position when it is placed in the classified (competitive) service or otherwise made subject to competitive examination acquires, on the agency head's recommendation, the rights of a competitive appointee, provided (a) six months' satisfactory service before and sixty days after the change, (b) noncompetitive tests of fitness, (c) no disqualification; opening words of the second proviso on conferring classified status. Ended with the whole order: EO 9830 Part III revokes it by number, effective 1947-05-01 under EO 9830's enacting clause. The order has no sunset, term or termination clause of its own. The time conditions in the text (six months' service, sixty days thereafter, recommendation within one year of reinstatement) are eligibility conditions for status, not ends of the order or report deadlines, so neither pending ruling is relied on. No amendment, extension, suspension or earlier partial end of this clause by any other instrument was found before 1947-05-01 (D6), so no later event is attached.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: corrected-6-cont: Rest of new Rule II sec. 6: in conferring classified status the Commission may waive physical requirements for long and faithful service and may count time on the Employees' Compensation Commission rolls as service; persons who left covered positions for military or naval service may acquire status on reinstatement on recommendation within one year and six months' meritorious service; persons failing the requirements may be retained without status but not promoted, transferred or assigned. Ended with the whole order: EO 9830 Part III revokes it by number, effective 1947-05-01 under EO 9830's enacting clause. The order has no sunset, term or termination clause of its own. The time conditions in the text (six months' service, sixty days thereafter, recommendation within one year of reinstatement) are eligibility conditions for status, not ends of the order or report deadlines, so neither pending ruling is relied on. No amendment, extension, suspension or earlier partial end of this clause by any other instrument was found before 1947-05-01 (D6), so no later event is attached.

ination: Provided:

satisfactory active service in such posi­
tion or in the civilian executive branch 
of the Federal Government immediately 
prior to the effective date of the change 
in status of the position, and continues 
to serve in such position for sixty days 
thereafter;
(b) That he shall pass such appro­
priate noncompetitive tests of fitness as 
the Commission may prescribe;
(c) That he is not disqualified by any 
provision of section 3 of Civil Service 
Rule V or of any other civil service rule 
or by any provision of the Civil Service 
Act or any other statute or executive 
order:
Provided further,  that in conferring 
a classified competitive status upon any

research_rationale: EO 8894 (signed 1941-09-08, 6 FR 4681-4682, FR issue of 1941-09-12), read in full from the held official FR text: enacting words and a rewrite of Civil Service Rule II sec. 6, printed across a page break, with a corrected inventory of two spans. It is revoked by number in EO 9830 Part III, effective 1947-05-01 (the enacting clause 'effective May 1, 1947' governs Part III; signing and FR filing on 1947-02-24 are not the effective date). The ACT record ACT:EO:8894>EO:9830 is an agent-located record upheld by an independent AI reviewer with a D6 step (simulated ingestion; not yet in the committed build). D6 / earlier-end test (did any instrument other than EO 9830 end the order or a clause before 1947-05-01?): The order has no sunset, term or termination clause of its own. The time conditions in the text (six months' service, sixty days thereafter, recommendation within one year of reinstatement) are eligibility conditions for status, not ends of the order or report deadlines, so neither pending ruling is relied on. The by-number scan of held FR order texts 8895-9860 finds no citation of 8894 other than EO 9830's Part III row; the OFR catalog records only the EO 9830 revocation. Every held 1941-1947 'Rule II' hit was read: EO 9230 (Board of Legal Examiners, 1942) twice applies 'Section 6 of Civil Service Rule II' to attorney positions (status after six months on compliance with sec. 6; noncompetitive examination prescribed with the Board's approval). That applies the rule as it stood and neither amends nor suspends it. No held instrument amends 'section 6 of Civil Service Rule II' after 1941-09-08 (the phrase occurs only in EO 8894 and EO 9230).
